metric: SolverKit stepper throughput relative to explicit-euler (relativeToEuler)
provenance: P7.31. Appended by `node scripts/plot-benchmark-trend.mjs --record`, which is a DELIBERATE LOCAL ACT: CI runs this script without --record, because a write in the runner's workspace is discarded (P0.102, and the same note on bench:throughput in ci.yml). CI's deliverable is the uploaded chart, not a grown history. Only `ratios` is charted and alerted on. `stepsPerSec` is carried for context where it was recorded and is never compared: it is a property of the machine. `machineId` is what makes two points comparable. It is NOT decoration -- measured 2026-09-19, classical-rk4 reads 0.44-0.49 on this container against the 0.2484 recorded in July, and dopri5 0.18-0.25 against 0.1364, so benchmark-baseline.json's claim that the ratio is 'largely hardware-invariant' does not survive contact with a second machine. Every ratio is compressed toward 1 here, which is what happens when per-step overhead rather than rhs evaluation is the larger share of a step. The alert thresholds are set from a measured table rather than declared: over these seven same-machine runs, taking every subset of a given size as the reference median and every remaining point as the latest, the worst downward excursion ON NOISE ALONE is -26.8% at two reference samples, -26.0% at three, -21.7% at four, -16.8% at five and -12.9% at six. regressionPct=30 clears the worst of those, not merely the one matching minSamples=5, because the large-reference rows are estimated from very few subsets.

samples.note: Carried over from scripts/benchmark-baseline.json, which is the only recorded run predating this file. The machine it was taken on is not recorded anywhere, so its machineId says so rather than guessing -- which is why it forms a segment of its own and never acts as a reference for a later point.
